3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Every spring, the seaside town of Sallabes celebrated the Scarlet Kingbird Festival.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: The vibrantly colored songbirds spent their winters in Xina, near the southern part of what used to be the Mousser Empire. Every spring, like clockwork, they flew back over the Gulf of Moridia to settle in Sallabes.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Their return was celebrated with music, dancing and lavish banquets, opened by a speech from the reigning Count or Countess of Sallabes. It was traditional for the King of Rizia and his family to attend.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: The sun hung low in the sky over the Arena Sallabes, a hundred-year-old open-air venue perched directly on the beach. Vina and I sat waiting in the royal box as cameras flashed in our direction.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: My daughter impatiently tapped her fingers on the arm of her chair. We hadn't spoken much since Iza.

9.speaker: Player_Romus
9.text: "I promise I won't try to shoot any of the birds."

11.speaker: Player_Romus
11.text: "Sit still. Can't you see everyone's watching?"

12.speaker: Player_Romus
12.text: "Are you corresponding with Rico these days?"

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: The audience roared as Manus Sazon got onstage.

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: He waited for the applause to subside, then held up a hand for the audience to listen. The entire arena fell silent.

16.speaker: Manus Sazon
16.text: "The story of the scarlet kingbird is a story about trust."

17.speaker: Manus Sazon
17.text: "He doesn't know what perils await him on the way to his destination, nor what sort of welcome will await him there. Yet he flies on, because something deep within his soul compels him to do so."

18.speaker: Manus Sazon
18.text: "Every year, this tiny feathered creature travels thousands of kilometers to reach our shores."

19.speaker: Manus Sazon
19.text: "And what of those who wait for him? They have no idea where he's been, or how he knows to navigate to this exact same spot each time. Still they gather here, scanning the skies for the first sign of his return."

20.speaker: Manus Sazon
20.text: "An inner voice that tells him, 'This is your home.'"

22.speaker: Player_Romus
22.text: "I wish he'd get to the point."

23.speaker: Player_Romus
23.text: "This is so maudlin. Why is the crowd eating it up?"

26.speaker: Narrator
26.text: Vina glared at me, then turned her full attention back to the man on stage.

27.speaker: Narrator
27.text: As if on cue, a solitary bird came flying towards us from over the horizon. Its plumage was bright red.

28.speaker: Narrator
28.text: A tear rolled down Manus' cheek.

29.speaker: Manus Sazon
29.text: "Trust. It's the only way any of this works. Even when we've been given no reason. Even when our faith is tested, over and over."

30.speaker: Narrator
30.text: A second bird followed, then a third.

31.speaker: Vina Toras
31.text: "A little bit. He says Bruno's running almost as fast on three legs as he did on four."

35.speaker: Vina Toras
35.text: "What? No, I was about ready to murder him after the Iza trip."

39.speaker: Vina Toras
39.text: "Yes, I can see everyone watching me. Same as yesterday, and tomorrow."

43.speaker: Vina Toras
43.text: "Sorry. Just excited to see the birds."

44.speaker: Manus Sazon
44.text: "It's only when we place our trust in one another that we are able to find our way."

45.speaker: Narrator
45.text: The audience gasped as the sky over our heads filled with hundreds and hundreds of kingbirds, their crimson feathers magnificently lit by the setting sun.

46.speaker: Player_Romus
46.text: "Keep your head down, Vina. Too much trust will get you a face full of shit."

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: Vina sniffled. She had tears in her eyes as well.

49.speaker: Player_Romus
49.text: "Have you ever seen anything so beautiful?"

51.speaker: Player_Romus
51.text: "Timing the speech perfectly with the migration? What a cheap trick."

52.speaker: Vina Toras
52.text: "I don't see anything cheap about it."

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: Once the sun had set and the birds had gone to roost, we made our way to the VIP reception in the neighboring pavilion.

54.speaker: Player_Romus
54.text: "A simple message. But you can't deny the truth in it."

56.speaker: Narrator
56.text: A big band was playing jazz music as Vina and I entered. We immediately found ourselves surrounded by local officials, celebrities and members of the press.

57.speaker: Narrator
57.text: It was nearly an hour before I was able to sit down. Almost as soon as I parked myself in a chair, I noticed Manus Sazon making his way over to me.

58.speaker: Player_Romus
58.text: "Mr. Sazon. A pleasure to see you again."

59.speaker: Player_Romus
59.text: "That was some speech today. I see why your constituents love you."

60.speaker: Player_Romus
60.text: "Not in the mood to dance, Mr. Sazon?"

61.speaker: Narrator
61.text: Manus smiled and shook my hand.

62.speaker: Manus Sazon
62.text: "A relief to hear, Your Majesty. I wasn't sure what to think after our last meeting."

63.speaker: Narrator
63.text: Manus smiled and bowed his head.

64.speaker: Manus Sazon
64.text: "The birds did most of the heavy lifting. But thank you, Your Majesty."

65.speaker: Vina Toras
65.text: "Rico wrote me that Bruno is back on his feet. Well, three of them."

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: She pointed to a cluster of buildings a little further down the coastline. In the middle of it rose a spire covered in scaffolding.

71.speaker: Manus Sazon
71.text: "I'm better off on the debate floor than the dance floor, Your Majesty."

72.speaker: Manus Sazon
72.text: "Actually, I've been hoping to speak with you for a long time."

73.speaker: Player_Romus
73.text: "That seat is reserved for my daughter."

74.speaker: Narrator
74.text: Manus gestured across the room. Vina was standing by the bar, having an animated conversation with the Derdian bartender.

75.speaker: Manus Sazon
75.text: "With your permission, Your Majesty, I'd like to keep it warm for a moment."

76.speaker: Narrator
76.text: He took a measured sip from the wine glass he was holding.

77.speaker: Manus Sazon
77.text: "But I still think we have a chance to accomplish great things for this country."

78.speaker: Manus Sazon
78.text: "As I said, I am not my father. Another revolution would damage the country and endanger what's left of my family."

79.speaker: Player_Romus
79.text: "Why? What exactly is it that you want?"

80.speaker: Player_Romus
80.text: "You assumed wrong. I don't intend to give up a single one of my powers as king."

81.speaker: Player_Romus
81.text: "So you are telling me you have absolutely no intention of doing away with the monarchy?"

82.speaker: Player_Romus
82.text: "I'm sure you're aware that removing any of the nobility's privileges would invite the wrath of all three royal houses. Yours included."

85.speaker: Vina Toras
85.text: "I was just speaking to the bartender. He's still trying to get the rest of his family out of Derdia. I told him I'd see what I could do."

86.speaker: Manus Sazon
86.text: "That's very noble of you. But there are thousands like him, and not all of them are lucky enough to catch the Princess of Rizia at a benevolent moment."

88.speaker: Vina Toras
88.text: "Your speech was beautiful, Mr. Sazon. Actually, it reminded me of an essay of Queen Lyza's from 1883--"

90.speaker: Manus Sazon
90.text: "'On Social Contracts.' Yes, that was one inspiration."

94.speaker: Vina Toras
94.text: "Your speech was beautiful, Mr. Sazon. Actually, it reminded me of something from a book I read recently."

95.speaker: Manus Sazon
95.text: "Really? I'd love to hear more about it."

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: The band began playing "Sweetheart of Ventrie City", an upbeat tune that had recently reached us from Arcasia.

97.speaker: Vina Toras
97.text: "You know what? I'll tell you after this dance."

98.speaker: Narrator
98.text: The band began playing "Sweetheart of Ventrie City," an upbeat tune that had recently reached us from Arcasia.

99.speaker: Vina Toras
99.text: "You know what? Tell me after this dance."

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: She took a step closer towards Manus and extended a hand to him. He looked at me questioningly.

101.speaker: Vina Toras
101.text: "Wait, this is faster than the dances I've been learning. Do you know the steps?"

102.speaker: Manus Sazon
102.text: "As a matter of fact, I do. I'll walk you through it."

103.speaker: Narrator
103.text: If he did, Vina didn't notice. Cameras flashed as the two of them started dancing.

107.speaker: Narrator
107.text: It was the same one her mother had given me during our first dance together.

108.speaker: Narrator
108.text: In all the years I'd been with Lena, my wife had never looked at me that way.

109.speaker: Player_Romus
109.text: "They are, and I wish I had time to act on them. But there are international crises that require my full attention."

110.speaker: Manus Sazon
110.text: "The kind of reforms I'm suggesting can keep Rizia stable through such crises."

111.speaker: Manus Sazon
111.text: "Just know that should you choose to guide Rizia in a more democratic direction, my party is prepared to back you."

116.speaker: Narrator
116.text: She pointed to a cluster of buildings a little further down the coastline. In the middle of it rose a spire covered in scaffolding.

118.speaker: Vina Toras
118.text: "It looks Dastnurist. I wonder if that's the sanctuary the Grand Wiseman was asking for."

119.speaker: Player_Romus
119.text: "Hmm. I thought it would be smaller."

120.speaker: Player_Romus
120.text: "It's a big, expensive building for heretics."

121.speaker: Narrator
121.text: I remembered my orders to fund the construction of an expanded Dastnurist Grandsanctuary in Sallabes.

122.speaker: Player_Romus
122.text: "That ought to keep the Wehzeks out of trouble for a while."

123.speaker: Player_Romus
123.text: "Sal was right. Everyone deserves a space to worship God in their own way."

128.speaker: Vina Toras
128.text: "And after that, another state function, and another..."

129.speaker: Vina Toras
129.text: "The program announced a special guest. I wonder who it'll be."

133.speaker: Narrator
133.text: He led Vina out onto the dance floor. I could swear he had the faintest hint of a smirk on his face.

134.speaker: Narrator
134.text: He led Vina out onto the dance floor. Cameras flashed as the two of them started dancing.

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: I wondered if the photographers were capturing the look in my daughter's eyes.

136.speaker: Narrator
136.text: This was no longer the nervous young man I'd met in Porte Drazon. He radiated confidence as he stepped up to the podium.

137.speaker: Player_Romus
137.text: "I'm sorry I haven't visited the House of Delegates yet. It's been a busy time."

138.speaker: Manus Sazon
138.text: "I understand, Your Majesty. The Zille incident rattled us all. My family included."

139.speaker: Player_Romus
139.text: "To be perfectly honest... I've been avoiding you. Too much bad blood."

140.speaker: Manus Sazon
140.text: "I understand. But isn't that precisely *why* we should talk?"

142.speaker: Player_Romus
142.text: "Do not address my daughter with such impudence, Mr. Sazon."

143.speaker: Player_Romus
143.text: "He's right. We've got to tackle this problem at the root, not by granting special favors."

144.speaker: Player_Romus
144.text: "How drunk are you, Vina? You can't go around making promises to random cater-waiters."

145.speaker: Player_Romus
145.text: "Forgive me, Mr. Sazon, but the Princess and I have really got to be going."

148.speaker: Vina Toras
148.text: "He was speaking to me as an equal, Father. I welcome his opinions."

153.speaker: Player_Romus
153.text: "You don't need my permission. Have fun out there."

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: Vina beamed. Manus took her hand and rose from his seat.

157.speaker: Narrator
157.text: Vina fixed me with an indignant stare.

159.speaker: Vina Toras
159.text: "We're guests here, Father. It'll look bad if we leave without engaging with our hosts."

161.speaker: Player_Romus
161.text: "I've engaged with our host enough. We're going. Now."

165.speaker: Player_Romus
165.text: "There will be other chances. Let's go."

167.speaker: Narrator
167.text: Vina let out an exasperated sigh.

168.speaker: Vina Toras
168.text: "I do apologize, Mr. Sazon. It's been lovely to spend time in your family's province."

170.speaker: Narrator
170.text: He took Vina's hand and pressed it to his lips.

171.speaker: Manus Sazon
171.text: "Until next time, Your Highness. Your Majesty."

172.speaker: Narrator
172.text: I saw her sneak a look back at him as we left the ballroom.

176.speaker: Narrator
176.text: It was a look I knew well. I'd seen it in her mother's eyes the day we first met.

181.speaker: Player_Romus
181.text: "Stop trying to ambush me, Mr. Sazon. Whatever you want, I'm not interested."

185.speaker: Player_Romus
185.text: "So why didn't you request an audience with me?"

186.speaker: Narrator
186.text: He gave me a look that was equal parts hurt and puzzled.

187.speaker: Manus Sazon
187.text: "I did, through your Grand Vizier. The message must have gotten lost."

188.speaker: Manus Sazon
188.text: "Please, Your Majesty. Just give me five minutes."

189.speaker: Manus Sazon
189.text: "But since we're both here right now, Your Majesty..."

190.speaker: Player_Romus
190.text: "Who's speaking to me right now? The heir of House Sazon or the speaker of the Rizian People's Party?"

191.speaker: Player_Romus
191.text: "All right, I'll indulge you. Tell me what you have in mind."

192.speaker: Player_Romus
192.text: "You have some nerve even approaching me after what your father did."

193.speaker: Manus Sazon
193.text: "I don't expect you to forgive Lucas Sazon. I haven't forgiven him myself."

194.speaker: Manus Sazon
194.text: "I used to hate him for robbing me of my birthright. Now, I realize his real crime was robbing Rizia of the peaceful transition it deserved."

196.speaker: Manus Sazon
196.text: "I joined the House of Delegates because of Lucas Sazon. Because my father's rash act of violence robbed Rizia of the peaceful transition it deserved."

198.speaker: Manus Sazon
198.text: "The rest of the RPP and I are in agreement. Our kingdom thirsts for reform. We can grant our people a voice without spilling a drop of blood."

199.speaker: Player_Romus
199.text: "You mentioned a transition. But a transition to what?"

200.speaker: Player_Romus
200.text: "The kind of change you're talking about doesn't happen peacefully. Look at how many corpses the Century of Revolutions left in its wake."

201.speaker: Manus Sazon
201.text: "It didn't have to be that way. If the kings and queens of your father's generation had been willing to compromise, they might have kept their crowns."

202.speaker: Manus Sazon
202.text: "Quite right, Your Majesty. With just a few changes, it can fulfill its intended purpose."

203.speaker: Narrator
203.text: Manus traced the rim of his wine glass with his finger.

204.speaker: Manus Sazon
204.text: "I heard your coronation speech. I believe your aims are the same as mine."

208.speaker: Manus Sazon
208.text: "I don't want to make assumptions... But could it be that your aims are the same as mine?"
208.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Coronation_Speech_AntiMonarchy"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.LeaningValue_Democratic"] > 0  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn02_Intention_ConstitutionalMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Focus_Government_Reform"] == true)

209.speaker: Manus Sazon
209.text: "I envision a Rizia where the concerns of commoners and nobles are given equal weight. Where an elected parliament makes the laws, but the royals retain their status and influence."

213.speaker: Player_Romus
213.text: "Why? The people of Rizia have everything they want. And if they want more, I'll give them more."

215.speaker: Manus Sazon
215.text: "There are factions within Rizia that have other, more radical ideas. The RPP and I are keeping them in check. For now."

216.speaker: Manus Sazon
216.text: "I know what you and your family think of me. And I know that my position in government is symbolic at best."

217.speaker: Player_Romus
217.text: "And House Sazon? What do your relatives think of your crusade against their kind?"

218.speaker: Narrator
218.text: Manus traced the rim of his wine glass with his finger.

219.speaker: Manus Sazon
219.text: "My crusade is not against the nobility, Your Majesty. It's on behalf of all Rizians."

220.speaker: Manus Sazon
220.text: "That's why any reforms we implemented would have to proceed very gradually."

221.speaker: Manus Sazon
221.text: "I would never presume to tell the King how the country should be run."

222.speaker: Manus Sazon
222.text: "Certainly not, Your Majesty. Preserving the status of the Rizian nobility is as much in my family's interest as it is yours."

223.speaker: Manus Sazon
223.text: "They want to be heard, Your Majesty. Not placated."

224.speaker: Player_Romus
224.text: "A second uprising will not happen during my reign."

225.speaker: Manus Sazon
225.text: "The commoners are tired of a ruling class that places its own desires above their own."

227.speaker: Player_Romus
227.text: "'For now'. Is that supposed to be a threat?"

228.speaker: Player_Romus
228.text: "It's not your job to keep them in check. It's mine."

229.speaker: Player_Romus
229.text: "That's the right idea. Without an outlet for their demands, they could become dangerous."

230.speaker: Player_Romus
230.text: "Hypothetically, if I, the King of Rizia, asked you to assist me in the complete dismantling of the monarchy, would you?"

232.speaker: Player_Romus
232.text: "I am more interested in knowing that House Sazon won't rise against me again."

233.speaker: Manus Sazon
233.text: "I know I am taking a risk by suggesting this to you. But I believe that unless significant changes are made, we may face another uprising."
233.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Coronation_Speech_AntiMonarchy"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.LeaningValue_Democratic"] > 0  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn02_Intention_ConstitutionalMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Focus_Government_Reform"] == true) == false)

234.speaker: Manus Sazon
234.text: "I do not doubt the strength of your regime, Your Majesty."

235.speaker: Manus Sazon
235.text: "But the commoners are tired of a ruling class that places its own desires above their own."

236.speaker: Manus Sazon
236.text: "But the longer our people are silenced, the louder they will be when they finally speak."

238.speaker: Player_Romus
238.text: "I don't like what you're implying. I would advise you to choose your next words very carefully."

239.speaker: Player_Romus
239.text: "What in the hell do you mean by that? I have only ever had my people's needs at heart."

240.speaker: Player_Romus
240.text: "I am looking forward to working more closely with your party to better serve our people. But changing the entire system of government? We probably won't go that far."

241.speaker: Manus Sazon
241.text: "My house has learned its lesson, Your Majesty. As long as you treat its members with dignity, they will be among your most loyal supporters."

242.speaker: Player_Romus
242.text: "I agree with the idea of reforming Rizia and empowering our legislative body. It is my wish that we work together to make it a reality."

243.speaker: Narrator
243.text: Manus' eyes lit up. He smiled confidently.

244.speaker: Manus Sazon
244.text: "We can discuss this back in the capital, Your Majesty."

247.speaker: Player_Romus
247.text: "I appreciate the risk you took in coming to me. It can't have been easy."

249.speaker: Manus Sazon
249.text: "We will get the public on your side. When the time comes, they will embrace reform without hesitation."

250.speaker: Player_Romus
250.text: "We should end this conversation before I'm obliged to have you arrested for treason."

252.speaker: Narrator
252.text: He took a handkerchief out of his pocket and dabbed his brow.

253.speaker: Manus Sazon
253.text: "I obviously chose the wrong venue for this conversation."

255.speaker: Narrator
255.text: He took a handkerchief out of his pocket and dabbed his brow.

256.speaker: Manus Sazon
256.text: "Please forget I brought this up with you, then.."

257.speaker: Player_Romus
257.text: "There is no right venue. You shouldn't have bothered me in the first place."

258.speaker: Player_Romus
258.text: "No, please go on. What were you going to tell me?"

259.speaker: Manus Sazon
259.text: "Of course. But will your successor? Or your successor's successor? We've seen how risky it is to let the fate of the country rest on a single ruler."

260.speaker: Player_Romus
260.text: "My house was chosen by God to rule, Mr. Sazon. Are you saying God made a mistake?"

267.speaker: Player_Romus
267.text: "It's nothing personal. But consider this topic off-limits."

269.speaker: Narrator
269.text: He stood up and pushed back his chair.

270.speaker: Manus Sazon
270.text: "If you'll excuse me, Your Majesty, I'm going to refresh my drink."

271.speaker: Narrator
271.text: He turned around to head to the bar and came face to face with Vina, who was returning to our table.

274.speaker: Manus Sazon
274.text: "Nothing to excuse, Your Highness. I hope you're enjoying your time in Sallabes."

278.speaker: Manus Sazon
278.text: "Thank you. I won't trouble you again."

279.speaker: Player_Romus
279.text: "Don't try to disguise your power grab as altruism, Mr. Sazon. I can see right through you."

281.speaker: Player_Romus
281.text: "What are you implying about my daughter, Mr. Sazon? You believe she's unfit to rule?"

282.speaker: Narrator
282.text: A tentative smile appeared on Manus' face.

283.speaker: Manus Sazon
283.text: "Come to the House of Delegates. You should have an idea how the current system works before we begin talking about how to fix it."

284.speaker: Player_Romus
284.text: "And I suppose your solution to that would be to make yourself Prime Minister?"

285.speaker: Manus Sazon
285.text: "I promise you, this is not about what I want. It's about securing the stability of the kingdom."

286.speaker: Player_Romus
286.text: "I agree that my government could be doing more for the non-noble classes."

287.speaker: Manus Sazon
287.text: "I understand, Your Majesty. Of course my party would be thrilled to have your ear."

288.speaker: Manus Sazon
288.text: "It would be an honor to see you at the next House of Delegates session."

291.speaker: Player_Romus
291.text: "Don't get too excited. I'm not promising anything yet."

292.speaker: Narrator
292.text: With a smile, he stood up and pushed back his chair.

293.speaker: Manus Sazon
293.text: "I've taken up enough of your time. If you'll excuse me, I'll freshen up my drink."

295.speaker: Player_Romus
295.text: "I understand what you're saying. But now is not the right time to start changing the status quo."

296.speaker: Narrator
296.text: A disappointed look spread across his face.

297.speaker: Manus Sazon
297.text: "If not now, then when, Your Majesty?"

298.speaker: Player_Romus
298.text: "Don't push me, boy. I've given you enough of my time this evening."

299.speaker: Player_Romus
299.text: "If and when the Zille crisis is solved, we may be able to revisit the topic."

300.speaker: Player_Romus
300.text: "I don't know. I'm sure you understand it's a lot to think about."

302.speaker: Narrator
302.text: A look of frustration spread across his face.

303.speaker: Manus Sazon
303.text: "Of course. Forgive me if I overstepped."

309.speaker: Vina Toras
309.text: "At least Bruno is adjusting well to life with us. The chefs have him spoiled rotten."

313.speaker: Vina Toras
313.text: "A little bit. He wanted to know how Bruno was doing at the palace. I told him the chefs have him spoiled rotten."

330.speaker: Player_Romus
330.text: "A giant flock of birds, migrating from a distant land... where have I seen that before?"

331.speaker: Vina Toras
331.text: "I don't know, Father. It's a beautiful sight, though."

333.speaker: Player_Romus
333.text: "Indeed. Like you, I sense a sea change coming to Rizia."

339.speaker: Manus Sazon
339.text: "The undercurrents to which I refer are like a river. They cannot be stopped, only channeled."

344.speaker: Manus Sazon
344.text: "With the new hydroelectric project you've approved for my province, I believe you know something about that."

346.speaker: Manus Sazon
346.text: "Which reminds me, I heard the royal government is considering a new hydroelectric project in this province. My relatives would be exceedingly grateful if it were to be implemented."

350.speaker: Manus Sazon
350.text: "I'm not convinced that's what the people of Rizia want at this particular moment."

352.speaker: Player_Romus
352.text: "The people have a voice. That's what the House of Delegates is for."

356.speaker: Manus Sazon
356.text: "You've implemented some of our proposals already. I'm glad you're open to working with us."

359.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
359.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Welfare_FreePress"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Welfare_AffordableHousingInitative"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Economy_GovernmentStimulusForPeople"] == true) == false

360.speaker: Manus Sazon
360.text: "It would help if you implemented some of the decrees we've proposed."

361.speaker: Narrator
361.text: A fanfare sounded from the pit orchestra, and a dark-haired woman stepped on stage. I recognized her as Leona Sazon, Countess of Sallabes.

363.speaker: Leona Sazon
363.text: "It is my great pleasure to welcome His Majesty King Romus and Her Highness Princess Vina to our humble city."

364.speaker: Leona Sazon
364.text: "We have another special guest here today as well."

365.speaker: Leona Sazon
365.text: "It has been 25 years since my beloved cousin Angelica was sent into exile. Like all Sazons, I hold out hope that someday, the King in his infinite generosity will bring her back to us."

366.speaker: Player_Romus
366.text: "Hmm. Perhaps the Sazon matriarch has been punished for long enough."

368.speaker: Player_Romus
368.text: "The only way Angelica is returning to Rizia is in a coffin."

369.speaker: Narrator
369.text: Vina ignored me. She craned her neck to get a better view of the stage.

370.speaker: Player_Romus
370.text: "I'm bored already. When do we eat?"

371.speaker: Narrator
371.text: Vina nodded. She craned her neck to get a better view of the stage.

372.speaker: Leona Sazon
372.text: "Today, we are graced with the presence of her child Manus. Heir of House Sazon, leader of the Rizian People's Party and prodigal son of Brenas."
